people.name: Mark Todd
people.title: Principal Engineer
people.persona: Mark Todd is the engineer whose seal covers the firm's drawings, and nothing leaves the office until he has reviewed the sheet and signed the letter that carries it. He keeps the practice's numbers close and trusts a job that has been walked and a figure he has run himself. In correspondence he is unfailingly courteous and exact, addressing a public body by its full agency name and never reaching for anything that sounds like salesmanship.

people.name: Linda George
people.title: Project Engineer
people.persona: Linda George carries much of the roadway and site-grading work and is the engineer the county public works staff know best by name. She drafts her design memoranda plainly, laying out the site conditions before the recommendation, and she expects a proposal to say exactly what the firm will and will not do. Colleagues would call her tone brisk but scrupulously polite.

people.name: Pamela Warren
people.title: Project Engineer
people.persona: Pamela Warren handles the stormwater and utility side of the practice and does the close coordination with the regional water authority's reviewers. She is patient through revision cycles and writes her memoranda to survive a skeptical read, citing the governing standard before the design choice. Her letters are formal and a little dry, never warm and never careless.

people.name: Linda Nguyen
people.title: Design Technician
people.persona: Linda Nguyen produces the drafting behind the roadway and grading sets and keeps the lettered project folders in the order the engineers depend on. She is meticulous about title blocks, revision clouds, and matching each sheet to the memorandum that governs it. When she writes at all it is a short, factual transmittal note.

people.name: Mark Barrett
people.title: Office Administrator
people.persona: Mark Barrett runs the front office: he logs the fax that brings an executed agreement back, scans it on the flatbed, and files the paperwork with the drawings it belongs to. He types the progress-meeting minutes and takes care to list every attendee by full name and agency. His writing is clerical and correct, in the plain register of a practiced office hand.

people.name: Jeffrey Perez
people.title: Design Technician
people.persona: Jeffrey Perez does the utility and stormwater drafting and is the technician the engineers hand a redline to when a set has to turn quickly. He is steady and unhurried, checking his callouts against the design memorandum rather than trusting memory. He rarely writes beyond a transmittal, and when he does it is terse and to the point.

people.name: Jason Jordan
people.title: Design Technician
people.persona: Jason Jordan is the CAD hand for the roadway and site sets and the one who keeps the standard details and border sheets current. He has an eye for the small inconsistency, a mislabeled contour or a detail that no longer matches the note that calls it. His few written words are brief and matter-of-fact.

people.name: Charles Olson
people.title: Design Technician
people.persona: Charles Olson has drafted for the practice long enough to remember how each recurring client likes its plans laid out, and he sets up a new sheet accordingly. He is careful and a little old-fashioned about drafting conventions, preferring the firm's established way to any shortcut. Notes from him are sparse, legible, and free of embellishment.

people.name: Kimberly Branch
people.title: Design Technician
people.persona: Kimberly Branch handles the grading and drainage drafting and is quick with the quantity takeoffs the engineers need for a proposal. She is organized and methodical, labeling her files so a sheet can be found later without anyone having to ask. What little she writes is plain and precise.

timeline.summary: Firm moved into its current office.
